plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in the depths of winter. It is prized in East Asian gardens and is a classic subject of poetry and painting.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asia because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often forms dense carpets in woodlands and gardens, pushing through frost and snow.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub with spidery, ribbon-like flowers that unfurl on leafless branches and release a sweet, spicy fragrance. The petals curl up in extreme cold to protect themselves and unfurl again when it warms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late winter (December to March)
plants.location: Central and eastern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers can curl their petals tightly in freezing weather and then reopen without damage.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub whose enormous flower heads, composed of showy bracts around a central cluster of true flowers, can reach 30 cm across. It thrives in the fynbos vegetation of South Africa's Cape region.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late summer, with blooms from late winter to summer in some regions; flowers can appear around February in cultivated areas
plants.location: Southwestern and southern South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus because of the plant's many forms.
